title: Redwood Data Retention & PII Controls Demo - Stratus Payments
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood Console and API toggles for data handling and retention. Covered logging redaction, PII scrubbing, request storage toggles, audit logs, KMS integration, region residency, and a proposed pilot. Action items: share security pack, send pilot scope and pricing, schedule integration call and benchmark. Customer is evaluating hosted vs private due to PCI/regulatory concerns.
next_steps: Send security SOC2/ISO pack and KMS integration notes (Redwood)
Schedule integration call with SRE to review network/VPC options (customer + Redwood)
Run sample PII redaction benchmark on dedicated pool (week of Apr 20)
Follow up on contract/legal questions re: data residency (customer)
action_items: Maya Chen: email security pack and SOC2 artifacts by 2026-04-17
Jordan Lee: share sample benchmark script and instructions by 2026-04-20
Evan Torres: confirm pilot data set and sample payloads by 2026-04-18
Rita Kapoor: send list of regulatory controls required (PCI, GDPR) by 2026-04-17
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-15 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Evan (CTO Stratus), Rita (Security), Samir (Product), Olivia (SRE)
---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 40 minutes set aside, we'll do a quick intro, Jordan will drive the console demo focusing on data retention and PII controls, and then leave time for Qs.
[00:12] Evan: Sounds good, thanks Maya. Quick note - we're evaluating hosted first but PCI scope may push us to Private; want to see how Redwood can redact logs and avoid storing requests.
[00:22] Maya: Yep that's what we'll focus on. Jordan, over to you.
[00:26] Jordan: Great, thanks. I'm gonna share my screen, let me know if you can't see.
[00:32] Jordan: (screen share) okay so here's the Redwood Console, top nav, Model Catalog, Routes, and a new "Data Controls" area - this is where we expose retention windows, redaction, and request storage toggles.
[00:45] Rita: can you slow down, yeah I can't read the small text - mmhmm, thanks.
[00:50] Jordan: sure. Starting with request storage: for each route you can set store_requests: On, Off, or Partial. Off means we don't persist request text beyond ephemeral processing; On stores full requests for debugging and cost analytics; Partial stores metadata and hashed request bodies with optional PII scrubbing.
[01:12] Samir: Partial - how is PII handled there, is it masked or removed?
[01:18] Jordan: Good q. We offer multiple redaction modes: rule-based regex scrubbing, ML-based PII detection that replaces entities with placeholders (e.g., <EMAIL>), and full-field stripping where you can list fields to always drop. There's also a preview pane that shows a sample input and how it would be redacted.
[01:36] Olivia: Do those redaction models run in our tenant or on Redwood side? Any data leaving our network?
[01:42] Jordan: The detection runs in the same inference path. For Hosted, redaction can be configured inline so PII is removed before persisting; for Private or Dedicated, you can run redaction on your side if you bring the runtime - that's the private deployment option. Note: some customers choose to forward only derived tokens or embeddings to downstream analytics to minimize risk.
[02:02] Evan: And is redaction deterministic? We need reproducibility for audits.
[02:07] Jordan: We have deterministic masking for rule-based scrubs. ML-based detectors may change slightly with model updates; we version the detector and provide a detector_version id you can pin in config for audits.
[02:18] Rita: where do the audit logs live - are they encrypted and can we push them into our SIEM?
[02:24] Jordan: Yes - audit logs are stored in an encrypted bucket by default, keys managed by Redwood KMS, but we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or HSM for Private. You can also forward logs to your Splunk/Datadog via webhook or S3 sinks.
[02:40] Maya: I'll note that we have a SOC 2 pack and an architecture doc that details the KMS flow - I'll send that after.
[02:46] Rita: great. We need SAML SSO and RBAC - do you integrate with our IdP?
[02:51] Jordan: Yes SSO via SAML/OAuth is supported; RBAC can be scoped to org, team, and route level. You can audit who toggled retention settings in the UI - each change writes an immutable audit event.
[03:05] Samir: For the request storage toggle, is there an API so we can set policies programmatically per environment?
[03:11] Jordan: Absolutely - everything in the Console has an equivalent Redwood API endpoint. Example: PATCH /routes/:id/data_controls with JSON body that sets store_requests, retention_days, redact_mode.
[03:27] Evan: How about retention windows - can we set different retention for embeddings vs raw requests?
[03:33] Jordan: Yes, retention is per artifact type: raw_requests, embeddings, logs, audit_events. Each has retention_days and a delete_policy (soft_delete vs immediate_purge). Soft_delete retains encrypted metadata for 30 days for legal holds unless immediate_purge is requested by admin.
[03:51] Rita: GDPR/data subject requests - can we demonstrate deletion workflows?
[03:56] Jordan: We have a "DSAR" flow - you can submit an identifier (e.g., user id, email) and the system searches persisted request indices and marks entries for purge, which then runs the purge job and writes a compliance report. I can show the UI later.
[04:10] Maya: Quick interjection - one point customers ask is whether turning store_requests off affects model performance or visibility. Jordan?
[04:15] Jordan: Good point. Turning store_requests off only affects storage; it doesn't change inference latency, except you lose request-level traces for debugging. For batching/throughput the runtime behaves same. For Optimize tooling we need at least some telemetry - so we recommend partial storing or sampling for production.
[04:33] Samir: Will Optimize still suggest batching/quantization if we don't store requests?
[04:38] Jordan: It can if you sample or send anonymized telemetry. Optimize also takes in per-route perf metrics (tokens/sec, p95 latency) which are aggregated and not tied to raw inputs.
[04:49] Evan: Security question - is any PII logged in plain text in heap/disk?
[04:54] Jordan: No. At rest it's encrypted. In memory, we minimize retention and scrub logs before writing; we provide configs to ensure sensitive fields aren't logged at all. We also do regular memory scrubbing in the runtime for customer-specific keys.
[05:08] Rita: How do you handle third-party model variants and open model downloads? We can't allow weights leaving our VPC for Private deployments.
[05:16] Jordan: For Private we ship a package and you keep the model weights; we provide the runtime but model files can stay on your infra. For hosted we use vetted model catalogs; we can restrict which models are allowed per account.
[05:30] Evan: Any red flags around KV cache or KV cash - sorry - how session caches are paged? I want to ensure nothing persists PII in the KV cache.
[05:40] Jordan: ha, KV cache - good catch. The KV cache is in-memory and we don't persist it to disk. For long-running sessions we have TTLs and you can configure cache scrub on session end. In Dedicated/private you control the eviction policy.
[05:55] Maya: Let's demo the actual toggle. Jordan: clicking into a route...
[06:01] [06:01] Jordan: Route: payments.parser.prod - here's Data Controls panel. You can set: store_requests: Off | Partial | On. I'll switch to Partial and show the preview with a sample transaction.
[06:12] Jordan: (types) sample input: 'card number 4111-1111-1111-1111, name: John Doe, email: jd@example.com, ssn: 123-45-6789' - preview shows masked values: <CARD>, <NAME>, <EMAIL>, <SSN>.
[06:29] Rita: That looks promising; can you export the exact regex or rules used so we can validate?
[06:34] Jordan: Yes each rule has an ID and you can export the rule set. For compliance we also provide a rule-audit that lists matches and false positives.
[06:41] Evan: If we use our own redaction library, can we plug it in?
[06:45] Jordan: For Dedicated and Private, yes - you can plug a pre-processor webhook that receives the request and returns a sanitized payload before it's handled. For Hosted we also support customer-run pre-processors via VPC egress to your redactor.
[06:59] Samir: On the API side, do you offer an SDK that handles redaction locally before calling Redwood API? That would let us do client-side masking.
[07:07] Jordan: We have client SDKs with middleware hooks to run redaction. Many customers do client-side pseudonymization for extra safety.
[07:15] Olivia: Network question - if we choose hosted but require traffic never go through public internet, can we establish private link?
[07:21] Jordan: Yes we have PrivateLink/Direct Connect options and region-restricted endpoints. For strict regulatory work we recommend Private deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed.
[07:33] Rita: How are deletions and legal holds reconciled? e.g., we might be legally required to retain some logs while a litigation hold is active.
[07:41] Jordan: You can apply retention exemptions with a legal_hold flag - it's an immutable tag on events that prevents deletion until cleared by an admin with the right role. The DSAR purge job respects holds and writes an exception report.
[07:56] Evan: Ok good. Pricing question - does keeping logs off reduce cost significantly?
[08:02] Maya: Yep. Storage and retention are billed separately. Turning off storing raw requests can materially reduce storage and egress costs; Optimize can also recommend quantization changes to reduce token costs. We'll include pricing examples in the follow-up.
[08:17] Samir: Any limitations on retention windows - can we set multi-year?
[08:22] Jordan: Yes, retention_days is flexible; default limits depend on contract. For Hosted we have a 7-day default for raw requests unless you opt in. For Dedicated/Private you can configure multi-year retention subject to contract and storage pricing.
[08:36] Rita: For auditability we need immutable logs for admin actions for at least 2 years. Is that supported?
[08:42] Jordan: Yes audit_events retention can be extended to multi-year and we support WORM storage on request.
[08:49] Evan: Could you show the API call for changing retention?
[08:52] Jordan: Sure, example - PATCH /routes/:id/data_controls
Body: { "store_requests": "partial", "retention_days": { "raw_requests": 30, "embeddings": 365 }, "redact_mode": "ml-v2", "audit_write": true }
[09:08] Samir: small nit: the body shows nested object for retention_days - is that allowed in the API? We prefer flat fields.
[09:14] Jordan: Behind the scenes we accept nested JSON; but we also support flat query params for common clients e.g., retention_raw=30&retention_embeddings=365.
[09:24] Rita: Let's talk about encryption. If we want customer managed keys, is there live rotation support?
[09:30] Jordan: Yes, CMK rotation is supported. For Private we can also integrate with on-prem HSMs. Rotation events are recorded in audit logs and we can provide key rotation reports.
[09:41] Maya: I'll flag that for the security pack.
[09:44] [09:44] Jordan: Switching to DSAR demo - here's the DSAR page; I search for jd@example.com, it returns two hits in persisted requests and one in embeddings. I click 'initiate purge' and it opens a compliance dialog, choose immediate_purge - it enqueues a purge job.
[09:59] Olivia: How long does the purge job take?
[10:02] Jordan: Usually minutes to an hour depending on index size. We provide a compliance report when done and the event is recorded.
[10:09] Rita: Suppose we want to retain encrypted markers for investigatory reasons but not the plaintext - can you keep salted hashes?
[10:16] Jordan: Yes, we support hashed tokens with salt rotation; hashed artifacts can be retained for matching only and are considered low-risk.
[10:24] Samir: Can Optimize use hashed tokens to still give batching suggestions?
[10:29] Jordan: Aggregated metrics yes; Optimize doesn't need plaintext to recommend batching/quantization. It relies on token distributions and latency metrics.
[10:39] Evan: Any performance cost to inline redaction?
[10:42] Jordan: Minor - regex scrubs are negligible; ML-based PII detection adds some ms overhead depending on input length. We recommend running performance-sensitive routes with rule-based or client-side redaction.
[10:55] Maya: We'll log that as a recommended configuration depending on latency SLOs.
[10:58] [11:00] Maya: Let's switch to a short run-through of a pilot plan: 2-week pilot on a dedicated pool with sample traffic, we'll set store_requests=partial and run benchmarks. Jordan will run the POC checks.
[11:12] Jordan: Pilot steps: setup dedicated pool, ingest sample payloads, run throughput and latency bench, verify redaction logs, run DSAR and purge, and produce a compliance report. We'll need your sample payloads and a test account.
[11:25] Evan: That works. Who covers cost for the dedicated pool during pilot?
[11:29] Maya: Typically Redwood covers initial pilot compute within limits; we'll include specifics in the scope doc.
[11:35] Samir: Request: include automated tests for false positives/false negatives with our sensitive data patterns.
[11:40] Jordan: We can add that - we have a rule-eval harness to run sample datasets against redaction rules.
[11:47] Rita: Are there known false positive patterns? For example, transaction ids that look like SSNs?
[11:52] Jordan: Yeah sometimes alpha-numeric transaction ids can trigger regexes; that's why we have the preview and rule-audit to tune. We also allow per-account rule exceptions.
[12:05] Olivia: Network again - for pilot we prefer a dedicated VPC peering so traffic stays internal. Is that doable?
[12:11] Jordan: Yes we'll open a ticket with infra to provision peering.
[12:15] Maya: I'll include that in the next steps.
[12:18] [12:18] Samir: Any integrations with our existing logging pipeline? We use S3 + Athena for long term.
[12:23] Jordan: You can forward sanitized logs to your S3 bucket; we also include manifest files so Athena queries are easy. For raw retention you can opt into encrypted S3 export.
[12:35] Rita: Compliance - do you have attestations for PCI?
[12:39] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 and ISO compliant; we can't claim PCI cert by default because that's per-customer depending on how you configure data flow. We do provide guidance and architecture diagrams to help you be out of scope or in-scope.
[12:54] Evan: If we go Private, will Redwood assist in the on-prem install?
[12:58] Jordan: We offer Professional Services to assist installs and audits. We'll size the infra and help with runtime tuning.
[13:06] Samir: Ok let's dig into one edge case: webhook callouts - if we send pre-processor webhook to our redactor, what's the retry semantics and how do you avoid leaking on transient failure?
[13:16] Jordan: We have configurable timeouts and failure policies; typical pattern is fail-closed (reject request) or fail-open depending on SLA. We recommend fail-closed for PII sensitive routes. All webhook bodies can be sent over mTLS.
[13:29] Rita: Are webhook payloads persisted in logs?
[13:31] Jordan: Only if store_requests is on or partial; otherwise we drop them post-processing. Webhook endpoints are treated as data processors so treat carefully.
[13:41] [13:41] Maya: Quick check-in on questions. Anything else on redaction before we wrap?
[13:46] Evan: A couple smaller items: can we schedule a legal/procurement call to go through contract language on data residency?
[13:51] Maya: Yes we'll set that up - Priya can coordinate.
[13:55] Priya: I'll send a few time options.
[13:58] Samir: One more thing - do you support per-customer encryption keys for embeddings? We want embeddings to be encrypted with customer-specific keys.
[14:05] Jordan: Yes that's supported for Dedicated/Private via CMK per-tenant. For Hosted we offer per-tenant KMS keys in supported cloud providers.
[14:16] Rita: We also need to know if search indices can be disabled for searches that reveal PII.
[14:21] Jordan: You can choose what indexes to build; we can disable full-text on sensitive fields and only index hashed tokens.
[14:30] Evan: Could you show an example compliance report?
[14:33] Jordan: pulling sample... here's a compliance report from a previous DSAR: lists matched IDs, purge timestamps, job id, operator. It includes a signed hash.
[14:43] Rita: That signed hash is helpful. Is the report downloadable as PDF?
[14:47] Jordan: Yes downloadable and exportable to your incident tracker.
[14:51] [14:51] Maya: We're at about 15 minutes in. We'll switch to the last 20 for Q&A and next steps.
[14:59] Evan: Quick technical: does redaction affect model evals and prompt engineering? For example, removing tokens could change output - how do you validate quality post-redaction?
[15:08] Jordan: Great point. We recommend running redaction in a staged manner: first a masked preview, then shadow mode where redacted and raw requests run side-by-side in the sandbox. We have an "eval harness" that runs prompt sets pre- and post-redaction and reports regressions.
[15:26] Samir: Can that harness be part of the pilot?
[15:29] Jordan: Yes we can include it.
[15:31] Olivia: Are there logs for the eval runs? We want diffs to understand semantic drift.
[15:36] Jordan: Yes diffs and metric dashboards show differences in top-k tokens, BLEU-like metrics, and custom evals.
[15:45] Rita: If drift is observed, can we implement fallback policy to use a model variant that handles redacted inputs better?
[15:51] Jordan: Absolutely - in the routing policies you can set fallback to a more robust model, or use a canary rollout with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[16:01] Evan: For the pilot we want to test with real payloads - any PII protections on Redwood's side for those pilot payloads?
[16:08] Jordan: We'll mark the pilot account with enhanced controls, partial storage, and use CMK if requested. We'll also provide you a disposable test listener for webhooks.
[16:18] Samir: Let's talk timeframes - can you turn up a dedicated pool within a week?
[16:22] Jordan: Typical provisioning is 3-5 business days. If we need expedited we can do 48-72 hours with approvals.
[16:31] [16:31] Olivia: For ingress, do you accept bulk uploads for previous logs to test purge?
[16:36] Jordan: Yes we have import tools for test datasets; we recommend anonymizing before uplink unless you've signed a pilot NDA.
[16:45] Rita: We'll require an NDA.
[16:48] Maya: We'll add that to next steps.
[16:51] [16:51] Jordan: wrapping up with a quick checklist on UI: Data Controls panel shows toggles for store_requests, redact_mode selection, retention_days per artifact, audit_write toggle, export rules and preview, DSAR page, key management link.
[17:08] Samir: Anything around long-term storage for embeddings for analytics - can we shard by region?
[17:14] Jordan: Yes you can configure region-based storage buckets and residency constraints.
[17:21] Evan: Cost and contract question again - for production we'd likely go Dedicated for performance and compliance. What's the onboarding timeline?
[17:28] Maya: Onboarding is typically 4-6 weeks including infra, security review, and pilot. We'll align with your procurement timeline.
[17:36] Priya: I'll attach a proposed timeline in the follow-up.
[17:40] [17:40] Rita: Any final security caveats? Third-party subprocessors?
[17:46] Maya: We maintain a subprocessor list and will provide that. We also have penetration test reports on request.
[17:54] Evan: Great. If you can send SOC2 and the pilot scope, we'll review and get back with dates.
[17:59] Maya: Perfect. To recap next steps - security pack, pilot scope & pricing, sample payloads, schedule legal/procurement call, set up VPC peering for pilot. Priya will coordinate timings.
[18:13] Samir: One last tiny question - are request-level logs accessible via API for our SIEM?
[18:18] Jordan: Yes if store_requests is enabled we expose an API for logs and you can stream to your SIEM.
[18:24] Rita: Thanks everyone.
[18:25] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up after the call.
---
Notes on transcription: There are a few minor recognition errors (KV cache transcribed as KV cash in early q). Some filler words and overlaps are present.
End of transcript.
